title: 와, 눈이 오네요! 새로 알게 된 것에 반응하기
objective: By the end, you can form -네요, -(는)군요 and -(으)ㄴ/는데요 correctly with verbs, adjectives and nouns.
summary: Learn three sentence endings for reacting to something new, -네요, -는군요 and -는데요, and the differences between them.

task.title: Complete the reactions
task.line: Use the endings from page 1 to fill in, choose or fix each sentence.

forms.when: You see, hear, taste or feel something right now and react to it. The ㄹ at the end of a stem drops (멀다 → 머네요).
forms.means: Oh, …! / Wow, …! (I notice this right now)
forms.exampleMeaning: (Looking out the window) Wow, it's snowing a lot outside.

forms.when: You have just learned or figured out a fact, often from what someone told you.
forms.exampleMeaning: (After your friend says she walks her dog every morning) Oh, I see, so that's why you get up early every day.

forms.when: The same meaning as -는군요. Adjectives and nouns take no 는, except words that end in 있다/없다, which take -는군요 even when they are adjectives (맛있는군요).
forms.example: 아, 이 집은 냉면이 제일 유명하군요.
forms.exampleMeaning: (Reading the menu) Oh, I see, naengmyeon is this place's most famous dish.

forms.when: You are surprised or impressed and want the other person to react. It's often better than you expected.
forms.exampleMeaning: Wow, you speak Korean really well!

forms.when: The same meaning with adjectives. Use -은데요 after a consonant and -ㄴ데요 after a vowel. The ㄹ at the end of a stem drops (길다 → 긴데요).
forms.exampleMeaning: The room is bigger than I expected!

watchOut: 맛있은데요 (X) → 맛있는데요 (O): Words that end in 있다/없다 take -는데요, even when they are adjectives.
작는군요 (X) → 작군요 (O): Adjectives take -군요 with no 는, except 있다/없다 words, which take -는군요 (맛있는군요). Otherwise only verbs take -는군요.
살네요 (X) → 사네요 (O): A stem ending in ㄹ drops ㄹ before -네요 and -ㄴ데요 (길다 → 기네요, 긴데요).
학생네요 (X) → 학생이네요 (O): After a noun that ends in a consonant, add 이 (학생이네요, 학생이군요).
제 이름은 민준이네요 (X) → 제 이름은 민준이에요 (O): Use these endings only for something new to you, not for things you already knew.
exercises: Write the -네요 form of the word in brackets: ① 이 가방은 정말 ____ (가볍다) ② 우리 집에서 학교가 꽤 ____ (멀다) ③ (You see your friend's empty plate.) 벌써 다 ____ (먹다, past)

Write the -는군요 or -군요 form of the word in brackets: ① (You hear that today is a holiday.) 오늘은 가게가 다 ____ (쉬다) ② (A friend says the restaurant is always full on weekends.) 주말에는 사람이 정말 ____ (많다) ③ (A friend says his older brother teaches at a high school.) 아, 형이 ____ (선생님)
Write the -는데요 or -(으)ㄴ데요 form of the word in brackets: ① (Looking at a coworker's new phone) 와, 사진이 정말 ____ (예쁘다) ② (Watching a child sing) 아이가 노래를 잘 ____ (부르다) ③ 이 드라마 생각보다 ____ (재미있다)
Choose the correct form: ① 오늘 날씨가 (춥는군요 / 춥군요). ② 이 식당은 손님이 (많은데요 / 많는데요). ③ 저분도 우리 회사 (직원이네요 / 직원네요).
Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: ① 와, 그 모자 정말 멋있은데요. ② 동생이 정말 예쁘는군요. ③ 민수 씨는 회사 근처에 살네요.

Read the situation and complete the sentence with the ending in brackets: ① You thought the line would be long, but it's short. 생각보다 줄이 ____ (짧다, -(으)ㄴ데요) ② A friend says, "저 어제 이사했어요." 아, 어제 많이 ____ (바쁘다, past + -군요)
answers: ① 가볍네요 ② 머네요 ③ 먹었네요
① 쉬는군요 ② 많군요 ③ 선생님이군요
① 예쁜데요 ② 부르는데요 ③ 재미있는데요
① 춥군요 ② 많은데요 ③ 직원이네요
① 와, 그 모자 정말 멋있는데요. ② 동생이 정말 예쁘군요. ③ 민수 씨는 회사 근처에 사네요.
